design_criteria.water_quality_volume_method: Water Quality Capture Volume (WQCV) based on runoff from 0.6 inches of precipitation within the UDFCD boundary, representing runoff from frequent storm events such as the 80th percentile storm; remaining runoff after volume reduction is treated through capture and slow release of the WQCV.

November 2015 Urban Drainage and Flood Control District

UDFCD criteria are based on a Four Step Process focused on reducing runoff volumes, treating the remaining WQCV, stabilizing receiving drainageways and providing targeted source controls for post-construction operations at a site.
EURV represents the difference between the developed and pre-developed runoff volume for the range of storms that produce runoff from pervious land surfaces (generally greater than the 2-year event).

Water Quality Capture Volume (WQCV): This volume represents runoff from frequent storm events such as the 80th percentile storm. Within the UDFCD boundary, the WQCV is based on runoff from 0.6 inches of precipitation.
evidence.page_or_section: Common Stormwater Management Terms, Page 1-9; Section 4.2, Page 1-17

evidence.excerpt: permeable pavement systems with subsurface storage, bioretention, extended detention basins, sand filters, constructed wetland ponds, and retention ponds. Green roofs and some underground BMPs may also provide the WQCV
